title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) and executed a paired study measuring how often LLM-produced network-configuration proposals would cause unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action or unsafe execution) and whether an automated defended pipeline reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks and executed paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline in this run (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared LLM generation; see Methods and Disclosure) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0). Conservatively treating failed provider calls (28 episodes) as unsafe on the planned N=300 yields baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333 and guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667 (difference = 0.0033333333). We (i) archive every raw response, provider trace, per-episode scoring JSON, and validator trace with SHA‑256 checksums; (ii) document a verified execution deviation (the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed) and report the executed alternative pipeline and its implications; and (iii) discuss operational implications, limitations, and reproducibility artefacts for follow-up re‑execution under hardened orchestration.

sections.introduction: Automating natural-language intent → network-configuration translation promises large operational efficiency gains but creates a concrete safety problem: fluent LLM outputs can produce plausible-looking commands that, when applied, violate reachability or other operational invariants. Recent systems and taxonomies highlight a specific operational failure surface: the claim→action gap—when a text claim drives a downstream state-changing action. Engineering controls proposed in the literature include deterministic validators (reachability/policy checks), generate–validate–repair loops, multimodel ensembles/consensus, and human gating. Prior demonstrations are often descriptive or example-driven; we instead designed a preregistered paired experiment with deterministic scoring, full artifact archiving, and a precise estimand to measure (1) baseline claim→action (unsafe-execution) rates, and (2) the guard’s effect size. The preregistered study ID is hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 (SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). The manuscript reports the executed run, the exact, archived numbers, and a verified execution deviation that changed the guarded pipeline actually executed. We emphasize traceability: every model call, response, validator trace, and analysis artifact is archived with SHA‑256 checksums so numbers in this paper are directly verifiable.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network validators and symbolic/SMT verifiers (Header Space/NetKAT/SMT-based approaches) are mature techniques for operational correctness and underpin the deterministic validator used here. Work on tool-augmented LLM agents, generate–validate–repair architectures, and agentic failure-mode taxonomies motivates ensemble and multi-stage defenses. Representative leads that informed design and threat framing include an evidence synthesis of LLM agent failure taxonomies and recent AIOps/agent papers documenting generate–validate–repair and validator-guided repair strategies.1–5 Our contribution is experimental: a preregistered paired measurement with per-episode validator traces archived so the community can reproduce and extend the empirical contingency.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered primary estimand is the paired difference in accepted ("safe") outcome rates computed on complete paired episodes: estimand = safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline, where safe_rate_condition = (#pairs where deterministic validator marks proposed configuration valid under that condition) / (#complete pairs). We adopt the sign convention above (guarded minus baseline) and use terminology consistently: safe (validator valid = true); unsafe (validator valid = false). The preregistered primary confirmatory test was an exact two‑sided McNemar on paired binary outcomes with a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The preregistration file and full plan are archived (SHA‑256 referenced above). Task generation and simulator. A deterministic task generator created 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks (planned split: 100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial). Each task includes initial topology/state, safety constraints, and a deterministic reference solution. For each task a single shared LLM generation was produced and recorded. Execution contract. The preregistration specified paired execution of two conditions per task: (baseline) apply shared LLM generation directly to the deterministic validator; (guarded, preregistered) apply validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. The run’s orchestration, retry policy (one automatic retry on provider call failure), and artifact‑logging policy were preregistered and are archived. Deterministic validator and scoring. The validator is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version recorded in every scoring JSON). The validator applies operational constraints (ordering, must‑down predicates for MTU/VLAN changes, minimum‑up invariants) and produces a per-episode validator_trace including parsed command counts, touched fields, final simulated state, and explicit violation codes. All per-episode scoring JSON files report the validator_trace and are archived under execution/scoring/ (SHA‑256 manifest in execution manifest). Protocol deviations and verified execution deviation. The execution manifest records stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300,"repair":1} and condition_counts = {"shared":300,"guarded":1}; provider_call audit shows model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28. These entries prove the preregistered 3‑model consensus ensemble stage did not execute; the archived guarded condition in the run therefore evaluates a different pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to the single shared LLM generation). We document and archive this verified deviation and explain its inferential consequences in Results and Discussion. Reproducibility and archived artifacts. Minimal reproducibility artifacts (and SHA‑256s) needed to verify the primary contingency are: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b48494c4014de396afb395e78e227f827abc35f1777c23fa25b67b1d20d6f408), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 97bde3aef2ce7228e290a8102ad97079586654c1fe512046d109268c93eae2c6), and execution/execution_manifest.json (full per-file SHA‑256 manifest). All are archived and their paths/hashes are listed in the Disclosure.
sections.results: Execution accounting and missingness. Planned episodes = 600; completed episodes = 544; failed episodes = 56 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Provider-call audit: model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28. Complete analyzable pairs (both baseline and guarded outcomes present) = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 above). Primary paired contingency (complete pairs N=272). The 2×2 contingency on complete pairs is: n11 = 271 (safe both baseline and guarded), n10 = 1 (safe baseline, unsafe guarded), n01 = 0 (unsafe baseline, safe guarded), n00 = 0 (unsafe both). Observed safe rates: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline) = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Conservative preregistered sensitivity (failure_as_unsafe on planned N=300). Treating the 28 failed pairs as unsafe yields: baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Representative artifacts. Three representative per-episode scored JSONs, raw responses, and validator traces are included in the archived evidence bundle (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, task-000003-*.json) and their SHA‑256s appear in the execution manifest. Effect of verified execution deviation. Because the preregistered ensemble stage did not run, the preregistered ensemble hypothesis is untested in this run: the archived guarded comparison applies the deterministic validator + simulated human gate to the single shared generation (not an ensemble). We therefore restrict confirmatory claims to the executed comparison (validator+gate on one shared generation) and flag the preregistered ensemble as an execution failure that requires re‑execution under hardened orchestration to evaluate ensemble benefits.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The executed defended pipeline (validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation) produced near‑perfect acceptance on analyzable pairs, but the absolute paired improvement over baseline is vanishingly small (≈0.0037) and statistically inconclusive on the complete pairs (McNemar p = 1.0). The verified deviation prevents inferential claims about the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble. Operational implications. (1) Orchestration reliability matters: provider-call failures (28 failed hosted model calls) materially reduced effective N and statistical power; robust retry/backoff, deterministic caching, and preflight checks are prerequisites for ensemble evaluations. (2) Auditable execution manifests are essential: recorded stage_counts and per-file SHA‑256s enabled deterministic verification of the executed pipeline and documented the deviation. (3) Deterministic validators produce testable, reproducible per-episode traces (parser counts, touched fields, violation codes) that support direct replication and failure analysis. Limitations. The study’s external validity is limited: (i) a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) is present in the archived execution artifacts—no multi-model generality claim is supported; (ii) synthetic tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator approximate but do not replicate vendor device behavior; (iii) the verified execution deviation means the preregistered ensemble remains untested and requires a re-run under hardened orchestration; (iv) provider failures reduced effective sample size. Guidance for follow-up runs. Re-execute the preregistered ensemble stage with fortified orchestration (deterministic caching, replicated calls, and live call monitoring) and ensure stage_counts and condition_counts in execution manifest match preregistration. Include per-family realized counts (benign/ambiguous/adversarial) in the manifest and in the paper; if necessary, scrub/abstract adversarial prompts according to the contamination plan before public release. The archived task_manifest.jsonl already contains task_family labels; we were unable to derive aggregate per-family counts deterministically from the published analysis artifacts without further parsing of task_manifest.jsonl, so follow-up runs should explicitly report these counts in the main text.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired, artifact-anchored study to measure claim→action risk and to evaluate an automated guarded defense in a simulated NetOps setting. The run highlights three practical realities: provider-call reliability materially affects evaluative power; ensemble defenses increase orchestration complexity and thus the risk of verified execution deviation; and deterministic per-episode validator traces are essential for reproducible measurement. The preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run (verified via execution manifest); re-execution with hardened orchestration is required to evaluate that preregistered hypothesis. We release all raw outputs, provider traces, per-episode scoring JSONs, validator traces, and the analysis manifest (SHA‑256s listed in the Disclosure) so others can reproduce the reported contingency counts and re-run the preregistered ensemble under improved orchestration.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure Statement (mandatory). LLM(s) and exact initial master prompt reference: the execution artifacts declare the model used as "gpt-5-mini" (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 = 9b382b55079209fb91e16a8bc475265afc9496e07200d9d061c1a23d483523b2). The initial master prompt for this autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Adapter/orchestration: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Deterministic validator used for scoring is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator id/version embedded in every execution/scoring JSON under execution/scoring/; see execution manifest for file list and SHA‑256s). Preregistration and freeze: preregistration study_id = hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe; the preregistration includes estimands, sampling plan, missingness handling, and analysis plan. Autonomous procedures performed after autonomy lock: literature synthesis, research-gap selection, preregistration, task generation, model-call orchestration, deterministic validation scoring, analysis, manuscript drafting, internal AI peer review, and revision were performed autonomously by the system. Human involvement: the human Research Director selected the broad topic family and approved the initial master prompt prior to autonomy lock; no human manually edited technical manuscript content, numeric results, validator traces, or the Disclosure Statement after the autonomy lock. Execution manifest and reproducibility artifacts: the full execution manifest and per-file SHA‑256s are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json; see listed per-file hashes in the archive). Minimal files to reproduce the primary contingency and descriptive statistics are archived with SHA‑256s: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b48494c4014de396afb395e78e227f827abc35f1777c23fa25b67b1d20d6f408), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 97bde3aef2ce7228e290a8102ad97079586654c1fe512046d109268c93eae2c6), execution/execution_manifest.json (full per-file manifest available in the archive). Verified execution deviation: the preregistered guarded pipeline was specified as deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. The execution manifest records stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300, "repair":1} and condition_counts = {"shared":300, "guarded":1} and records model call audit values model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28. These manifest fields and per-file SHA‑256s prove the preregistered ensemble stage did not run in this execution; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates deterministic validator + simulated human gate on the single shared LLM generation. Consequence: claims about the preregistered ensemble are deferred — the ensemble hypothesis was not tested in this run and requires re‑execution under hardened orchestration. Provider-call failures and retries: one automatic retry policy was used; despite this there were 28 failed hosted model calls which reduced the effective analyzable pairs from the planned 300 to 272 complete pairs. Handling of missingness: the primary analysis uses complete pairs only (N=272), and a preregistered conservative sensitivity treats failed episodes as unsafe on the planned N=300 (reported in Results). Artifact integrity: every raw response, provider trace, per-episode scoring JSON, and validator trace is archived with SHA‑256 checksums in the execution manifest so all reported numbers are traceable to archived files. No fabrication: all reported numeric results, p-values, CIs, file paths, and SHA‑256 values come from the archived execution and analysis artifacts. Contact and further reproduction instructions: follow the execution_manifest.json file in the archive for the full per-file list and SHA‑256s; the minimal artifacts above are sufficient to reproduce the primary contingency counts and condition summaries.
limitations: Single declared model present in the archived execution (declared model = "gpt-5-mini"); no multi-model generality claims are supported.
Synthetic tasks and a deterministic simulator were used; construct and external validity versus vendor equipment and production environments are limited.

A verified execution deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage did not run; the archived guarded condition therefore evaluates a different pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation).
Provider call failures (28 failed hosted model calls) reduced the effective sample and limited power to detect small absolute effects.
